title: AI-Found Linux Kernel Flaw Gives Local Users Root, and Can Break a Guest Out to the Host
summary: A flaw in Linux's vhost subsystem lets a local user read and write kernel memory at will and become root across nearly a decade of kernel versions. In one virtualization setup, it lets an untrusted virtual machine write to the host's memory and hijack the program that runs the virtual machine.

title: Four-Byte Write and Timing Bug Let Researchers Run Code in Windows SmartScreen Enclave
summary: Security researchers ran their own code inside a protected part of Windows that is meant to stay sealed off even when the rest of the computer is taken over.
card_summary: Security researchers ran their own code inside a protected part of Windows that is meant to stay sealed off even when the rest of the computer is taken over.

sections.context: This reflects continued use of phishing as an initial-access path in broader intrusion chains.

email_summary: Security researchers ran their own code inside a protected part of Windows that is meant to stay sealed off even when the rest of the computer is taken over. The protected area is a VBS enclave, an isolated slice of memory the operating system uses to guard secrets, and the one they broke into handles passwords for a Windows anti-phishing feature.
